featured_reviews.name: KartiK Mittal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hidden haven in Bandra that feels like a deep breath

Stumbled upon this gem on the District app while wandering through Bandra. The Yoga House is one of those classic Bandra homes turned into a calm, airy cafe. You won’t spot a flashy sign from the road, so trust Google Maps and keep your eyes peeled for a quiet villa entrance. A staff member guided us upstairs. The first floor looks set up for yoga, and the cafe opens out on the second.

Seating is split into three moods. Indoors for soft light and calm conversations. A leafy outdoor section for sunshine and breezes. And one level up, a shamiana style nook where you sit cross-legged and forget time. It feels like a friend’s mindful terrace more than a commercial cafe.

We picked an outside table. Peaceful. Not crowded. Bandra energy without the traffic noise. Service was warm and unhurried. We tried their Summer Salad. Fruity, crunchy, and bright with mixed produce. Roughly ₹545 all in. Portion was decent and left us satisfied. Prices lean premium, but you are paying for the setting and the slow, healthy focus.

What I loved

1. Tucked away location that keeps it serene

2. Variety of seating that lets you choose your vibe

3. Staff that actually looks after you without hovering

Good to know:
•	Harder to spot from the street, so navigate straight to “The Yoga House” near Nargis Villa or Water Bungalow

•	Menu skews healthy and light. Great if that is your mood, not ideal if you want heavy mains

Verdict:
Come here when you need a gentle pause in the middle of Bandra. Perfect for solo journaling, slow brunch with a book, or a catch-up where you can actually hear each other. If you like trying unique, aesthetic spaces and don’t mind spending a little extra for quiet and quality, this one belongs on your list.

The group workouts are challenging but designed so everyone can work at their own level. The programming is varied—you never get bored, but there's enough consistency to track real progress. My personal trainer Viraj is exceptional - he not only took the effort to understand and program for my fitness goals but took the effort to understand who I am and what motivates me.

Most importantly, the Tribe has helped me rediscover my love for fitness.I genuinely look forward to showing up. Whether it's the high-fives after a tough workout, the supportive messages in our group chat, runners club or the community events - UTC, Match Day - they've created something special here. The emphasis and experience of community is amazing. Any trainer who may be at the studio when you are - will help you get stronger and better. Most people you work out along side will suffer with you and laugh with you - maybe you will make a new friend.

If you're looking for more than just a place to work out—if you want a supportive community that will celebrate your victories and push you when you just cannot or don’t want to—this is your place.

She keeps introducing new contemporary exercises (like planks, wall exercises, etc) and activities (like music therapy, candle-gazing, etc), to make the sessions more interesting and diverse. She also explains the benefits of various exercises and encourages us to practice them at home (although most of us rarely do so).

I recommend The Yoga Institute, Juhu to anyone looking for an engaging, value-for-money fitness option in the neighbourhood, especially for those who have never tried Yoga before.

featured_reviews.name: Shruti Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Training with Kunal over the past three months has been a transformative journey. My posture and endurance have significantly improved, but the most profound changes are internal. Kunal’s focus on the core builds strength, ensuring each new asana is introduced with careful, incremental steps that make even the most complex poses feel attainable. His unique ability to turn challenging asanas into achievable goals, combined with unwavering encouragement and positive energy, creates an inspiring atmosphere. Whether in one-on-one sessions or group classes, his genuine care for his students radiates. I wholeheartedly recommend him to anyone ready to evolve both physically and spiritually.

featured_reviews.name: Himali Khabar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve always been more of an active person — dance, gym, outdoor workouts — and honestly, I used to think yoga was slow or boring (though I had never really tried it). On top of that, I had been away from any physical activity for the last few years due to slip disc, C-section delivery, and umbilical hernia surgery.

A few months ago, I got a chance to attend Kunal’s yoga class, and I must say — I was pleasantly surprised. It was a wonderful experience, definitely beyond what I imagined yoga to be. I came back home smiling, with a glow on my face.

There isn’t too much preaching about asanas — it feels like a beautiful blend of workout and the art of surrender. Kunal has this amazing aura that keeps you fully engaged in the class — your mind is completely present, nowhere else.

One thing I truly appreciate is his strong focus on technique. I like doing things properly, and Kunal teaches postures and asanas with great technical clarity, guiding you gradually and safely. Every session leaves you feeling satisfied and energized.

I would definitely recommend everyone to try his classes — especially if you think yoga isn’t for you. You might just surprise yourself like I did!

She always brings a variety of asanas to every session. Hetal mam is very punctual and professional. It’s been one month since we have been attending the class and we both are experiencing a visible difference in our energy levels, muscle strength, posture, and joint health. We are both extremely happy with Hetal ma'am and wish to continue to be her students. She is the best yoga teacher we have ever come across.
